hook: SAMPLE: how a chatbot remembers you

beats.say: Your chatbot doesn't actually remember you. Here's the trick.
Every time you send a message, the app quietly bundles the whole conversation so far and sends all of it back to the model as one long block of text.
The model reads that block from the top, every single time, and then predicts the next words of its reply.
That block has a size limit, called the context window, measured in tokens, which are small chunks of words. Early chat models held a few thousand tokens. Some newer ones accept 1,000,000 or more.
So what happens when a chat grows past the limit? Something has to give. Some apps drop the oldest messages. Others keep a short summary instead.
A few save key facts, like your dog's name, to a separate memory file and paste them back in later. Say 40% of a chat is small talk: that goes first.
So the next time an AI assistant recalls something you told it last week, it isn't remembering. It's rereading. Would you want it to forget on purpose?
